comment: The version sweep. versions.json compares two points — the release JBrowse 2
pinned in 2023 against the current one — which says how much faster the
parsers got but not where the change landed. This file names every major
line in between so the answer can be a curve rather than a ratio.
Selection rule: the newest patch of each major line, read off npm on
2026-08-16. Newest-patch rather than first-release of each major because a
major line accumulates fixes after its .0, and the last patch is the one that
line finally became; the first .0 would credit the next major with work its
predecessor shipped.
The rule has one consequence worth stating rather than discovering: the 2023
pins in versions.json are NOT sweep points. @gmod/bam v2.0.0 is the pin and
v2.0.4 is the sweep's major-2 point. They are close but not identical, so a
sweep row and a versions.json row for the same major are two measurements,
not one repeated. sweep.ts marks the major each 2023 pin falls inside.
A version that will not build from source with today's toolchain is recorded
as unbuildable and skipped, not fatal — setup.sh --sweep keeps going. Which
of a library's majors can still be built at all is itself a result, so it is
reported rather than silently dropped.
bgzf-filehandle and vcf-js are deliberately absent for now. Both are
measurable by the same driver — add a block here with the same shape and
sweep.ts picks it up — but the three libraries below are the ones whose
2023-to-current gap the render benchmarks actually sit on top of.
rule: newest patch of each major line, npm as of 2026-08-16

libraries.name: cram-js
comment: Every major before 8 defaults fetchSizeLimit to 3 MB and throws past it,
which every long-read window in this corpus exceeds. JBrowse 2 never ran
that default — its CramAdapter set 200_000_000 — so the arm passes the
same value to any version that accepts it. That is the identical
adjustment lib/corpus.ts already documents as OLD_CRAM_OPTS, applied
across the sweep rather than only to the 2023 point.

libraries.name: bbi-js
comment: The single-file BigWig case is 1-3 ms and versions.json reports it as
flat to slightly negative. Read the sweep here for shape, not for a
headline: cohort-bw.ts is where this library's cost becomes legible,
because a per-file fixed cost is what a signal panel pays 100 times.
